newsitem.title: CHINA: China may offer stock, bonds linked to dam project.
newsitem.headline: China may offer stock, bonds linked to dam project.

text.p: China may offer on foreign markets bonds or stocks linked to the huge Three Gorges dam project, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The newspaper did not say how much debt or equity might be offered abroad or specify which markets, saying only that this would depend on financial needs for the project and the state of international capital markets.

"Under the basic principle of keeping costs down, we would like to consider raising funds through various channels and by multiple means," the newspaper quoted Li Yongan, vice president of the Three Gorges Project Development Corp.
Li said that capital construction investment on the project had reached 17.3 billion yuan ($2.08 billion) by the end of September and that the project's budget was well under control.
The Business Weekly said the total cost of the project, expected to be completed in the year 2009, was estimated at 203.4 billion yuan.
It also said that profits from the Gezhouba dam, currently China's biggest hydropower station, have been channeled to the Three Gorges project.
The article suggested that the electricity sales from the Gezhouba dam would be used as income for any debt or equity issued on the Three Gorges project.
"The listing would liven up the potential of Gezhouba dam since the power station has long seen stable profits and reliable returns," the newspaper said.

The newspaper also said that around the end of this year, the Three Gorges Project Development Corp would offer one billion yuan worth of three-year domestic bonds to be listed on the nation's stock markets. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
